# Installing Plugins

One way to install plugins is to use a plugin manager like [dtomvan/xpm.xplr][1].

But you can also install and manage plugins manually.

## Install Manually

- Add the following line in `~/.config/xplr/init.lua`

  ```lua
  local home = os.getenv("HOME")
  package.path = home
  .. "/.config/xplr/plugins/?/init.lua;"
  .. home
  .. "/.config/xplr/plugins/?.lua;"
  .. package.path
  ```

- Clone the plugin

  ```bash
  mkdir -p ~/.config/xplr/plugins

  git clone https://github.com/sayanarijit/material-landscape2.xplr ~/.config/xplr/plugins/material-landscape2
  ```

- Require the module in `~/.config/xplr/init.lua`

  ```lua
  require("material-landscape2").setup()

  -- The setup arguments might differ for different plugins.
  -- Visit the project README for setup instructions.
  ```

## Luarocks Support

Some plugins may require [luarocks][2] to work.

Setup luarocks with the following steps:

- Install luarocks (via your package managers or follow the [official guide][2]).
- Add `eval "$(luarocks path --lua-version 5.1)"` in your `.bashrc` or `.zshrc`.
- Add the following lines in `~/.config/xplr/init.lua`

  ```lua
  package.path = os.getenv("LUA_PATH") .. ";" .. package.path
  package.cpath = os.getenv("LUA_CPATH") .. ";" .. package.cpath
  ```

  Now you can install packages using luarocks. Be sure to append `--lua-version`.

Example:

```bash
luarocks install luafilesystem --local --lua-version 5.1
```

[1]: https://github.com/dtomvan/xpm.xplr
[2]: https://luarocks.org
# Writing Plugins

Anyone who can write [Lua][1] code, can write xplr plugins.

Just follow the instructions and best practices:

## Naming

xplr plugins are named using hiphen (`-`) separated words that may also include
integers. They will be plugged using the `require()` function in Lua.

## Structure

A minimal plugin should confirm to the following structure:

```
.
├── README.md
└── init.lua
```

You can also use [this template][2].

### README.md

This is where you document what the plugin does, how to use it, etc.

### init.lua

This file is executed to load the plugin. It should expose a `setup()`
function, which will be used by the users to setup the plugin.

Example:

```lua
local function setup(args)
  local xplr = xplr
  -- do stuff with xplr
end

return { setup = setup }
```

## Publishing

When publishing plugins on GitHub or other repositories, it's a best practice
to append `.xplr` to the name to make them distinguishable. Similar to the
`*.nvim` naming convention for [Neovim][3] plugins.

Finally, after publishing, don't hesitate to
[let us know][4].

## Best practices

- Try not to execute a lot of commands at startup, it may make xplr slow to
  start.
- When executing commands, prefer `Call0` over `Call`, `BashExec0` over
  `BashExec` and so on. File names may contain newline characters
  (e.g. `foo$'\n'bar`).
- File names may also contain quotes. Avoid writing directly to
  `$XPLR_PIPE_MSG_IN`. Use `xplr -m` / `xplr --pipe-msg-in` instead.
- Check for empty variables using the syntax `${FOO:?}` or use a default value
  `${FOO:-defaultvalue}`.

## Examples

Visit [Awesome Plugins][5] for xplr plugin examples.

## Also See

- [Tip: A list of hacks yet to make it as Lua plugins][15]
- [Tip: Some UI and theming tips][12]
- [Tutorial: Adding a New Mode][6]
- [Example: Using Environment Variables and Pipes][7]
- [Example: Using Lua Function Calls][8]
- [Example: Defining Custom Layout][9]
- [Example: Customizing Table Renderer][10]
- [Example: Render a custom dynamic table][11]
- [Example: Implementing a directory visit counter][16]

[1]: https://www.lua.org
[2]: https://github.com/sayanarijit/plugin-template1.xplr
[3]: https://neovim.io
[4]: https://github.com/sayanarijit/xplr/discussions/categories/show-and-tell

A layout config contains the following information:

### CustomLayout

A whole custom layout to render. It doesn't make sense to use it as a
[Static][25] layout, but can be very useful to render as a [Dynamic][26] layout
for use cases where the structure of the layout needs to change without having
to switch modes.

> WARNING: Rendering the same dynamic custom layout recursively will result in
> a ugly crash.

#### Example: Render a custom dynamic layout

```lua
xplr.config.layouts.builtin.default = { Dynamic = "custom.render_layout" }

xplr.fn.custom.render_layout = function(ctx)
  local inner = {
    config = {
      constraints = {
        { Percentage = 50 },
        { Percentage = 50 },
      },
    },
    splits = {
      { Static = { CustomParagraph = { body = "Try your luck..." } } },
      { Static = { CustomParagraph = { body = "Press ctrl-r" } } },
    },
  }

  local layout_type = "Vertical"
  if math.random(1, 2) == 1 then
    layout_type = "Horizontal"
  end

  return { CustomLayout = { [layout_type] = inner } }
end
```

- **border_style** ([Style][33]): The style of the borders.

## Content Renderer

It is a Lua function that receives [a special argument][36] as input and
returns some output that can be rendered in the UI. It is used to render
content body for the custom dynamic layouts.

## Content Renderer Argument

It contains the following information:

- [layout_size][37]
- [screen_size][37]
- [scrolltop][57]
- [app][38]

### Size

It contains the following information:

- x
- y
- height
- width

Every field is of integer type.

### scrolltop

Type: integer

The start index of the visible nodes in the table.

### app

This is a lightweight version of the [Lua Context][39]. In this context, the
heavyweight fields like [directory_buffer][50] are omitted for performance
reasons.

Hence, only the following fields are available.

- [version][40]
- [pwd][41]
- [initial_pwd][53]
- [vroot][52]
- [focused_node][42]
- [selection][43]
- [mode][44]
- [layout][45]
- [input_buffer][46]
- [pid][47]
- [session_path][48]
- [explorer_config][49]

## Also See:

- [xplr.config.layouts][51]

def run_one(executable_cmd, keys_list, args="", outfile=None):

    snaps=[]
    snaps.append(("init", capture(), capture(e=True)))
    for label, keys in keys_list:
        send(*keys)
        snaps.append((label, capture(), capture(e=True)))
    return snaps

    ours = run_one("python3 /workspace/app_src/__main__.py", keys_list, args)

# ---------------- key handling ----------------
def handle_key_event(self, key):
    if key.get("code") == "mouse":
        return self._handle_mouse(key)
    mode_kb = self.mode.get("key_bindings") or {}
    gen_kb = self.config["general"].get("global_key_bindings") or {}
    merged = {}
    for k, v in (gen_kb.get("on_key") or {}).items(): merged[k] = v
    for k, v in (mode_kb.get("on_key") or {}).items(): merged[k] = v
    action = merged.get(key.get("name"))
    if action is None:
        action = self._category_action(key, mode_kb, gen_kb)
    if action is None:
        if self.config["general"].get("enable_recover_mode") and self.mode_id != ("builtin", "recover"):
            found = self.find_mode("recover", "builtin")
            if found is not None:
                return self._switch_mode(found)
        self.log_warning("key map not found.")
        return []
    return list(action.get("messages") or [])

def _category_action(self, key, mode_kb, gen_kb):
    cats = _key_categories(key)
    for field in cats:
        action = mode_kb.get(field)
        if action is None: action = gen_kb.get(field)
        if action is not None: return action
    # default
    action = mode_kb.get("default")
    if action is None: action = gen_kb.get("default")
    return action

def _handle_mouse(self, key):
    mouse = key.get("mouse") or {}
    b = mouse.get("button", 0)
    if not self.mouse_enabled: return []
    if b & 64:
        if b & 1:
            return self._msg_FocusNext(None)
        return self._msg_FocusPrevious(None)
    if mouse.get("pressed") and (b & 3) == 0:
        hit = getattr(self, "_hit_table", None)
        if hit:
            inner, offset, header_h, rows_area = hit
            x, y = mouse["x"] - 1, mouse["y"] - 1  # SGR is 1-based
            if inner.x <= x < inner.x + inner.w and inner.y + header_h <= y < inner.y + header_h + rows_area:
                idx = offset + (y - inner.y - header_h)
                if 0 <= idx < self.directory_buffer["total"]:
                    now = time.time()
                    last = getattr(self, "_last_click", None)
                    self._last_click = (idx, now)
                    if last and last[0] == idx and now - last[1] < 0.4:
                        return self._set_focus_index(idx) + self._msg_Enter(None)
                    return self._set_focus_index(idx)
    return []

def _key_categories(key):
code = key.get("code"); ch = key.get("char")
cats = []
if code == "char" and ch is not None:
    is_alpha = ch.isalpha(); is_num = ch.isdigit(); is_alnum = ch.isalnum()
    if is_alpha: cats.append("on_alphabet")
    if is_num: cats.append("on_number")
    if is_alnum: cats.append("on_alphanumeric")
    if not is_alnum: cats.append("on_special_character")
    cats.append("on_character")
    return cats
if code in ("backspace","left","right","up","down","home","end","page-up","page-down","back-tab","delete","insert","enter","tab","esc"):
    cats.append("on_navigation")
if code in tuple(f"f{i}" for i in range(1, 13)):
    cats.append("on_function")
return cats
# attach key handlers to App
App.handle_key_event = handle_key_event
App._category_action = _category_action
App._handle_mouse = _handle_mouse

I've completed the reimplementation. Summary of the work:

**Process:** I probed the original `xplr 1.1.0` binary extensively (CLI parsing order and error formats, `-m`/`-M` jf-template quirks and pipe-delimiter detection, serde_yaml-style message validation in its strict and lenient forms, TUI geometry/styles/scrolling measured at many terminal sizes, modes, search/filter/sort semantics, history handling, the Lua config system with version checks and the debug-error mode, environment variables/pipes, interactive file operations, and the full `PrintAppStateAndQuit` dump).

**Implementation** (from scratch, Python 3 stdlib only, in `app_src/`):
- A Lua 5.1 interpreter (lexer/parser/tree-walking evaluator with closures, metatables, `require`, and a standard library) plus the `xplr` Lua API including the full `xplr.util` surface
- A marked-value YAML parser/emitter reproducing serde_yaml output (the app-state dump is byte-identical to the original apart from nondeterministic HashMap ordering)
- The complete message engine (129 messages: focus/navigation, visited history & deep branches, selection, filters/sorters, fuzzy/regex search, modes/layouts, shell/Lua commands with pipe files and env vars, FIFO, vroot, quit variants)
- A terminal renderer (constraint-solving layouts incl. the table-column allocation, ANSI/LS_COLORS styling, input cursor) that matches the original screen output
- The default configuration extracted from the program's own state output

**Testing:** CLI regressions against saved original outputs, tmux-driven interactive flows (navigation, search accept/cancel, scrolling offsets, create/rename/delete via the interactive bash scripts, interactive `:!` shell, plugin loading via `require`, hooks, custom modes/renderers/layouts), and a fresh-clone `./compile.sh` build.

`compile.sh` builds `./executable` as a self-contained zipapp; it's executable, and `./executable`/`__pycache__` are covered by `.gitignore`. Changes are committed.
